Multisystem and single-system forms can involve many different sites, most commonly central and peripheral nervous system, skin, breast, bone, and lung

Lesional cells

Large histiocytes with round to oval vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli, abundant pale cytoplasm with indistinct borders and emperipolesis; minimal atypia and mitotic activity (Ki-67 < 10%)

Oval histiocytes with grooved, folded, or lobed nuclei with fine chromatin and delicate nuclear membranes, inconspicuous nucleoli, and moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm; minimal atypia although mitoses may be abundant

Histiocytes with single small nuclei and foamy, occasionally eosinophilic cytoplasm; frequent Touton giant cells

Large histiocytes with irregularly folded nuclei, fine chromatin, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, sometimes with minor emperipolesis

Histiocytes can be spindled or foamy, with or without admixed Touton giant cells
